x: David Main and Geoff. Pearson scored in all of our winning teams, whilst Tommy Clinton and Dick Tobin graduated from the "B" team in the South of the Thames "Junior" to the winning team in the National.
Derrick Burfitt, our junior champion, was an easy winner of the individual race, and he was followed home by two more club members, in Dave Main 2, and Geoff.
Len Herbert also ran well in 4th place, and then our two newcomers, Geoff. Pearson and Tom Clinton, came along together and the team race was assured.

We were wondering what had happened to Tom Carter, but he soon came along and although not running in his usual form, he was quite well up considering the class of the field. Dave Main was with Tom and Geoff. Pearson, Tom Clinton and Dick Tobin were all going strong.
However, bearing in mind the absence of Dave Main and Geoff. Pearson, and the mishap to Tom Carter, we can be quite satisfied with our lads' performances.

Surrey Colours were won by Tom Carter, Len Herbert, Bill Lucas and Leslie Stokell. Middlesex Colours by Vic Blowfield and Geoffry Pearson. In the Kent Championships George Lucas was 5th and in the Herts.

Our members in this race were representing Cadogan A.C., the holders of the title, but they sadly missed Dave Main, Dan Patience and Charlie Smart, and had to take third place in the team championship. Our members' positions and times were—8 G.
Running for Middlesex were Vic Blowfield, who had dropped out of the County race owing to shoe trouble, and Geoff Pearson, while George Lucas was in Kent colours, and A.

Stimpson 38th, our lads were third in the team race, and they sorely missed the help of Charlie Smart and Geoff.

George Chantler finished 6th but was running for our "B" team who were placed 4th while our "C" team finished 6th out of an entry of nine teams. On the 17th April in the Walton 10 miles race, Tom Clinton finished first with Tom Carter fifth, Geoff Pearson 14th and Bert Mitchell 16th.
Geoff. Pearson was sixth in the Inter-Banks Championship over 4½ miles at Hayes (Kent), and third in the Westminster Bank 5 miles Championship.

Our first man home was that old warrior Bert Footer and next came Geoff Pearson, whom we do not see very much these days. Dick Towndrow and George Chantler both retired and this left our "A" team with only two finishers.

Syd Ring was our first man home in 10th position, a very good performance, considering the opposition, and he was also the second Surrey man to finish in the Inter-County race held in conjunction. Geoff Pearson, running for the Westminster Bank, was the next Club member home and he was closely followed by A.
Con Abberton came next in 2 hrs. 56 mins. 40 secs. and then George Chantler 2 hrs. 59 mins. 34 secs. To beat 3 hours over this course was quite a good effort and others to finish were G.

Geoff Pearson gained standard award of 3 hrs. 50 mins., his actual time being 3.39.28, in the S.L.H. 30 miles road race. We congratulate Freddie Bradnum, now a B.B.C. producer in the Midlands, on finishing 12th in the recent Liverpool Marathon, and hope his duties will not prevent us seeing him at B…
McDonald 13; Dick Tobin 18; and Geoff Pearson 20.

Arthur Whitehead kept going well until about 23½ miles when he began to tire and then Geoff Pearson, who had run a good steady race, came through very strongly to catch Arthur on the track and to beat him into 2nd place in the Club Championship.
The Wandsworth Council promoted a 14 miles road run in connection with their Coronation celebrations, and Geoff Pearson finished 3rd, with Len Rolls 8th and Bert Smith 15th.
Bert has been running really well this year and might well have assisted our team which was also without the support of Bob Plummer and Geoff Pearson.
Jordan, 10th in 2.0.14 and G. Pearson 16th in 2.3.3., all within Southern Standard.
Bishop, G.Pearson and J. McDonald who all ran well enough to give us second team place to Walton A.C.

Colin gradually moved up to 9th, whilst Eric Gebbett, Bob Plummer and Geoff Pearson, who ran the race of his life, finished 14th, 18th and 19th respectively to give us a team victory of 38 points to 40 of T.V.H. and 48 for Walton.

The Southern 20 Miles Road Race was held on 5th May in conjunction with the Essex County Race at Brentwood, and our team was weakened by the absence of Colin Collis and Geoff Pearson, but we felt fairly confident of a place.
In addition to Collis, Gebbett and Plummer whose positions and times were given, the following members completed the course:- 44th. G.M.

We were also without the services of Geoff Pearson. However, with the minimum of three runners we did as well as could be expected, although Walton's margin over us was greater than the result would suggest, owing to the questionable practice of deleting individual positions when arriving at the team result.

Discretion was the better part of valour and the old hands Wally Wortley, Alan Bishop, Geoff Pearson, Alf Byford, Arthur Penstone and John MacDonald were making certain that their race would last the full distance - good team stuff !
Our fourth man at this stage was Alan Bishop in 55th place but he didn't stay there for long, and at nine miles was overtaken by Geoff Pearson.
Nearly ten minutes were to elapse before our next man, Geoff Pearson, put in an appearance, and his running enabled us to secure third place in the Open Team Race.

Ken Stimpson, Geoff Pearson and Pete Mathews were 23rd, 25th and 26th. when the fifty-six competitors remaining went out for the final lap. Pawsey was a comfortable winner in the 2nd. fastest time ever recorded, 1hr 51:06 and Cooke's 1hr 52:12 had been bettered on only three occasions.
At the same meeting Roger Hudson was our first lad home in the Boy's race, followed by J.Allan and young Pearson, whose action looks more like father Geoff's each time out.

John Moore was placed 6th at '20' with Stairs still behind him,but he faded a little,though,to put up the creditable time of 2:45:54 in 8th place over a very tough course. Stairs' time was 2:41:26 and Geoff Pearson was our 3rd scorer in 21st position with 3:03:27.

The Belgrave Team,running as Cadogan AC,finished 3rd in the Middlesex '20',held in conjunction with the Finchley Open '20'. John Hilton, Geoff Pearson and Ken Stimpson comprised the team . John's time completed his qualification for our 2nd class standard.

After going through 15miles in just over 84mins. he began to slow down quite a bit and John Moore, now beginning to get a little fitter, passed Charlie at about 21 miles and went on to take the Belgrave Championship Geoff Pearson and John Hilton ran well throughout John finishing in a personal best time.
Geoff Pearson, Alan Bishop and Len Bishop represented Belgrave in the second Oxfam Marathon, Alan completing his qualification for a Club second class standard.
Geoff Pearson was the sole representative of the Club in this race, finishing 31st.
Unfortunately Charlie was forced to retire at 20 miles and join the other victims, Norman Stairs and John Hilton thus leaving Geoff Pearson and Ken Stimpson to close in the team.
A friendly atmosphere prevailed in our opening match of the season at Epsom, with our opponents having a Belgravian flavour in the form of Alan Morrison, Geoff Pearson and Stan Bradshaw.
The 'old firm' of Ken Stimpson, Alan Bishop and Geoff Pearson ran through once again quite steadily but strongly - Geoff ought to know the way by now, he first ran the 'Finchley' in 1946!!
Alan Bishop was our fourth scoring man in the Open Race just getting the better of ever-green Geoff Pearson, who none the less ensured we had all our runners inside 3hrs.
Also, congratulations to Geoff Pearson who this year 'became of age' by running his 21st Poly Marathon - surely a record which will take some beating.
Having managed three in twenty there was now a long gap before Bill Matthews, Geoff Pearson and Don Bonser arrived almost together; some twenty minutes later Alan Bishop jogged happily in.
Together with the other three Clive formed the team which came second in the Open Team Race Later Ken Stimpson, Geoff Pearson and Don Bonser all arrived very tired and glad to see the finish.

Brian Joines passed Tony Brien in the latter stages to finish strongly whilst Geoff Pearson in his 22nd Poly improved on his time of last year by 4 mins-19secs (Ken Stimpson please note!!).

For the Bank, our newly elected life member, Geoff Pearson, was 28th in 41m. 50s. The race was also something of a City of London Police convention, with our own John Kelly and David Davies in the field, together with policeman Wilde, 36th in 46m. 41s.

These included Martin Best and John Wasbrough making their 20 miling debut and Geoff Pearson - still going well. Next year's race will be the 25th and to mark the occasion it would be an idea to give the first 25 finishers a prize.
His 32:08 was only a few seconds down on his March run when everyone is reckoned to be considerably faster and this gained him third handicap prize behind the racing Piddington and Geoff Pearson.

Our best wishes go to Geoff Pearson on his retirement from the National Westminster Bank. What does he go and do though, only a week into his retirement - He "crocks" his leg through piling on the extra training!

Belgrave narrowly missed the Surrey 3rd team medals but there was one Belgrave prize - Geoff. Pearson won the 'Over 50' Vets. prize with a time of 2hrs.34min.23 secs. - not bad at nearly sixty years of age!
Paul Pringle at 125th was pleased to get near the 3 hour barrier with 3:00:59, whilst Doug Maughan and Geoff Pearson ran to 3:10:47 and 3:32:31 respectively for their 153rd and 181st places.
